title: Norman and the Carrot Kingdom
subtitle: A small pony. An enormous appetite.
description: Norman the Shetland pony sets off to find the world's biggest carrots. Choose his path, help new friends and discover whether the Carrot Kingdom is really as crunchy as it sounds.

start.title: A Very Promising Leaf
text: Something green sailed over the paddock fence and landed on Norman’s head.
The green thing slid down his nose.
Norman sniffed it. Then he nibbled one feathery leaf, just to check.
A swallow swooped onto the fence.
“From the Carrot Kingdom. Beyond the hills. They’re gathering the harvest.”
Norman had heard the stories. Carrots as thick as fenceposts. Carrots as long as benches. Carrots so big that—
Then he looked at the leaf.
“You can follow the brook through the trees,” said the swallow. “Or take the windy path over the hill. Both lead to the valley.”
Norman tucked the carrot top beneath his headcollar.
He trotted towards the paddock gate, which was standing open.
“I am going on a quest,” he announced.
“That,” said Norman, “depends how much chewing there is.”

brook.title: The Cart That Wouldn’t
text: The brook chuckled over smooth stones.
Norman followed it beneath the willows, ducking under branches that would have tickled a taller pony’s ears.
Around a bend, he found a little wooden cart blocking the path.
An otter stood in front of it, pulling a harness.
“That’s the third radish I’ve lost. At this rate, I’ll arrive with a cart full of fresh air.”
“The Carrot Kingdom. I’m delivering lunch for the gardeners.”
“So am I,” said Norman. “Except for the delivering lunch part.”
Otter stood and brushed his paws.
“The wheel’s caught between those stones. I thought I could pull it through.”
Norman leaned closer. The cart was small enough for him to help pull, but there was also room to lower his head and inspect the wheel.
Behind the cart, the path was too narrow to squeeze past.
“We had better sort this out,” he said.
choices: Help Otter pull the cart free
Look for what is trapping the wheel

steady-pull.title: One, Two, Heave!
text: Otter fastened a spare strap to the cart.
The cart gave a tiny creak.
They pulled together, slowly and steadily.
The wheel climbed the edge of a stone.
With a bump and a rattle, the cart rolled free.
Norman sat down too, although he hadn’t meant to.
For a moment, they looked at each other.
Then they laughed so hard that another radish fell out.
Otter popped it back into the cart.
Norman nodded. He rather liked being part of a team.
At the next bend, Otter took the smooth delivery path beside the water.
“Your path goes up through those hazels. You’ll see the valley from the top.”

stuck-wheel.title: A Very Small Problem
text: Norman lowered his nose beside the wheel.
There was a large stone on one side.
Another large stone on the other.
A pebble had wedged beneath the wheel like a doorstop.
“It is doing a very good job.”
Otter fetched a stout stick from beside the brook. He eased it under the edge of the wheel while Norman watched the pebble.
Norman nudged the pebble aside with his hoof.
Then he gave the harness a careful tug.
“Oh!” said Otter, hurrying after it. “Oh, that’s much better!”
“I nearly pulled my whiskers off,” said Otter, “and all I needed was to look underneath.”
At the next bend, Otter took the smooth delivery path beside the water.
“Go up through those hazels,” he called. “The valley is just beyond.”
He kept an eye out for small things causing large problems.
Especially if they were sitting beneath his feet.

hill.title: A Pumpkin in the Way
text: The hill wind blew Norman’s mane over one eye.
The wind put it over the other.
Near the top stood a garden gate.
In the gateway sat a pumpkin.
Behind the pumpkin stood a sheep.
“Excellent. I’ve been trying to get this pumpkin to the Carrot Kingdom’s harvest picnic.”
She pushed it with her shoulder.
“I grew it on this side of the gate,” she explained. “That was my first mistake.”
The pumpkin had squeezed halfway through, but its lower half was pressed against a hump of earth. One side touched the gatepost.
“I could fit beside that post,” he said.
There was room for Norman to nudge the pumpkin while Sheep pushed. Or he could scrape away some of the loose earth underneath it.
Beyond the gate, the path continued towards the valley.
choices: Clear a path around the pumpkin

rolling-pumpkin.title: The Pumpkin Wobble
text: Norman squeezed beside the low gatepost.
His bottom fitted, although it required a little wriggling.
Norman pressed his shoulder against the pumpkin.
Norman stepped back for a breath. As he moved, the pumpkin rocked towards him.
Then they let it rock gently back.
The pumpkin rolled over the hump.
Norman scrambled out of the gateway.
The pumpkin rolled onto the level path and settled against a tuft of grass.
“Well! A little wobble was what it needed.”
Sheep fetched a low trolley from beside the fence. Together they rolled the pumpkin aboard.
“I’ll take the long path round,” she said. “You go straight over the ridge. And save me somewhere to put this!”
Behind him came the squeak of trolley wheels.

clear-path.title: Room for a Pumpkin
text: The earth beneath the pumpkin was dry and crumbly.
“I think it needs a little more room.”
Sheep fetched a short wooden rake from the garden.
She loosened the hump of soil while Norman scraped the crumbs away with his narrow front hoof.
They worked along the pumpkin’s lower edge.
Soon, a shallow groove ran through the gateway.
It rolled through the gate and settled on the path.
For a moment, Sheep stared at the empty space where it had been.
“I was trying to squeeze the pumpkin smaller.”
Sheep laughed and fetched a low trolley from beside the fence. Together they rolled the pumpkin aboard.
“I’ll take the long path round. Yours goes straight over the ridge.”
Norman brushed some soil from his hoof.
He hadn’t needed to be stronger than a pumpkin.
He had just needed somewhere to put it.
“See you at the picnic!” called Sheep.

kingdom.title: Bigger Than Norman
text: At the top of the ridge, Norman stopped.
Below him lay a sheltered green valley.
There were little doors in the banks, washing on tiny lines and rows upon rows of feathery leaves.
Some were taller than Norman’s ears.
At the bottom, six rabbits stood around a carrot with a rope tied beneath its leafy crown.
Nearby, other carrots lay ready for the harvest picnic. One was longer than a wheelbarrow. Another was as thick as Norman’s middle.
Then he walked around it again.
A rabbit in a floppy gardening hat waved.

variants.text: “I helped Otter free his cart,” Norman said at last. “We had to pull together.” The gardener looked at the rabbits, who were all tugging at different moments. “That sounds useful.”
“I helped Otter free his cart,” Norman said at last. “A tiny pebble was trapping the wheel.” The gardener glanced down at the soil. “Perhaps we should look more closely here, too.”
“I helped Sheep move her pumpkin,” Norman said at last. “A gentle rocking movement loosened it.” The gardener gave the carrot an interested look. “We’ve mostly been yanking.”
“I helped Sheep move her pumpkin,” Norman said at last. “We cleared some earth to give it room.” The gardener nodded. “This carrot does seem rather tightly packed in.”

text: “This is our biggest carrot,” said the gardener. “We’d love to share it at the picnic. Would you help?”
The rabbits had a broad pulling harness that would fit him. Beside the vegetable beds waited a row of small spades.
His stomach gave an enormous rumble.
kingdom.prompt: How should Norman help harvest the carrot?

ending-pull.title: The Great Carrot PLOP

variants.text: Norman remembered Otter’s cart. “We need to pull at the same time,” he said. “I know a good count.”
Norman checked around the carrot’s base. There was no loose pebble to nudge away this time. “Let’s try together,” said the gardener. “Slow and steady.”
“First, a little wobble,” said Norman. The rabbits helped him rock the carrot gently until the earth around it cracked.
Norman scraped a little loose soil from around the carrot’s crown. “That gives us some room.” The gardener nodded. “Now let’s pull together.”

text: The gardener fitted Norman’s harness and fastened it to the rope.
The rabbits lined up behind him.
Six pairs of rabbit ears tipped back.
Something deep beneath the ground made a sucking noise.
The rabbits tumbled into a soft, surprised heap.
And the carrot lay across the grass like an orange canoe.
For three whole seconds, nobody spoke.
Then Norman said, “I think that is bigger than me.”
The picnic blankets came out. So did bread, radishes, apple juice and enough carrot slices to make a crunchy orange mountain.
Norman’s slice hung over both sides of his plate.
“I knew it would fit,” he said.
The gardener looked at the plate.
Norman moved it onto the blanket.
When the evening shadows stretched across the valley, the rabbits packed him a parcel for home.
Norman tucked the enormous carrot top beneath his headcollar again.
This time, he knew exactly how big the carrot had been.
He had eaten some of it.
And there was still plenty left.

ending-dig.title: The Root of the Trouble

variants.text: “Pulling together helped Otter,” said Norman. “But you’ve already done a lot of pulling. Let’s see what’s underneath.”
Norman remembered the pebble beneath Otter’s wheel. “Before we try harder,” he said, “let’s find out what’s holding it.”
Norman gave the carrot a careful nudge. It barely wobbled. “That worked on the pumpkin,” he said. “This one needs a different idea.”
Norman remembered the groove beneath Sheep’s pumpkin. “Let’s make a little room,” he said.

text: They loosened the packed soil while Norman scraped it gently away from the edge.
Soon, a thick orange root appeared.
One root curved beneath a flat stone.
Two rabbits lifted the stone while the gardener carefully eased the root free.
They moved clear of the hole and took hold of the rope. With Norman in the harness and the rabbits pulling alongside, the carrot rose slowly from the earth.
Up came a long, curly tip.
The rabbits lowered it onto the grass.
Norman walked from one end to the other.
Soon, picnic blankets covered the lawn. There were radishes, warm bread and enough carrot slices for everyone.
The gardener handed Norman an especially generous piece.
Before he left, the rabbits packed a parcel for his friends at home.
Norman looked back from the valley path.
The empty carrot hole was almost big enough for a pony.
